rows.name: Top status bar fixed-text VRAM-buffer table (MARIO, WORLD, TIME)
rows.notes: PRG source of the fixed HUD words along the top of the screen. It is a WriteVRAMBuffer record stream: each record is [PPU addr hi, PPU addr lo, length, tiles...] and the buffer ends with a 0x00 first-byte terminator. Record 1 at prgRom 0x752: 20 43 05 then tiles 16 0A 1B 12 18 = 'MARIO' at nametable $2043 (row 2, col 3); record 2 at 0x75A: 20 52 0B then 20 18 1B 15 0D 24 24 1D 12 16 0E = 'WORLD  TIME' at $2052 (row 2, col 18); terminator 0x00 at 0x76B. Letter tiles: M=16 A=0A R=1B I=12 O=18 W=20 L=15 D=0D T=1D E=0E, blank=24. Proof: write_memory prgRom 0x755 (MARIO 'M' 16) -> 20 ('W'), ledger seq 1, reset_emulator, screenshot of the title screen HUD read 'WARIO'; undo_edit restored 16. The card's WORLD text is a different table (see world_card_text_table), so this edit did not touch it.

rows.name: WORLD-card text record ('WORLD 1-1' intro/death card)
rows.notes: PRG source of the black card that shows 'WORLD 1-1' after Start / on death. Record header at prgRom 0x783 is 21 4B 09: PPU address $214B = nametable 0 row 10, col 11, length 9. Data at 0x786: 20 18 1B 15 0D 24 24 28 24 = 'WORLD' + blank + a placeholder byte + '-' (28) + a placeholder byte; the world/level digits are patched into the two placeholder positions at runtime (observed card = WORLD 1-1 with 01 28 01). Confirmed the card position by reading nametable 0 while the card was up: row 10 cols 11-15 = 32 24 27 21 13 ('WORLD', same letter tiles as the HUD) and cols 17-19 = 01 28 01 ('1-1'). Proof: write_memory prgRom 0x786 (card 'W' 20) -> 16 ('M'), ledger seq 1, reset_emulator, pressed Start, screenshot showed the card read 'MORLD 1-1' while the top HUD still read 'WORLD 1-1'; undo_edit restored 20.

rows.name: ? block 16x16 metatile tile-id table entry (TL/TR/BL/BR = $53/$54/$55/$56)
rows.notes: PRG ROM source of the four 8x8 tile ids that make the 16x16 ? block. A table at prgRom 0xC80 (CPU $8C80), 4 bytes per 16x16 metatile (9 entries, 0xC80-0xCA3; followed by the palette blocks at 0xCA4); the ? block entry is 4 bytes at 0xC8C = 53 55 54 56 = $53,$55,$54,$56, stored in the order TL,BL,TR,BR. On screen in World 1-1 the ? block at NT1 col 25/26 row 10/11 sampled as TL=$53 (205,86), TR=$54 (211,86), BL=$55 (205,94), BR=$56 (211,94), all BG palette 3. There is a second identical entry at 0xC90. Proof (search and ledgered write): write_memory prgRom 0xC8C = $24 (sky) -> ledger seq 1 in hack eval-sheet2-tiles, reason '? block entry first tile $53 -> sky'; reset_emulator, Start + hold Right ~150 frames into 1-1, pause; screenshot showed every ? block on screen with its top-left quadrant replaced by sky; undo_edit restored $53 and a later level load showed the block whole again.

rows.name: small Mario standing-frame tile-id table entry (TL/TR/BL/BR = $3A/$37/$4F/$4F)
rows.notes: PRG ROM source of the four 8x8 tile ids that make small Mario's standing frame (sprite pattern table $0000, sprite palette 4). The table holds 8 bytes per frame: 4 tile ids used by small Mario (row-major TL,TR,BL,BR) plus 4 bytes that are $FC blank padding in the small-Mario frames. Small Mario's standing frame is the 4-byte run at prgRom 0x6ED3 = 3A 37 4F 4F = $3A,$37,$4F,$4F; the next frame (walk/airborne $9E,$9E,$9F,$9F) is at 0x6ECB, so the frames are 8 bytes apart (0x6E83, 0x6E8B, ... 0x6ED3, 0x6EDB...). Emulator observation before the edit: small Mario standing at the start of 1-1 emitted OAM entries tile $3A at (40,193) TL, $37 at (48,193) TR, $4F at (40,201) BL, $4F h-flipped at (48,201) BR, with two $FC blank padding rows above; when he was mid-air the frame switched to $9E,$9E,$9F,$9F, matching the 0x6ECB entry. Proof (search and ledgered write): write_memory prgRom 0x6ED3 = $FC (blank) -> ledger seq 1 in hack eval-sheet2-tiles; reset_emulator, Start, wait ~3.5 s for 1-1 and Mario to stand; pause; list_sprites then showed OAM index 5 (Mario's top-left) as tile $FC while $37/$4F/$4F were unchanged, and the screenshot showed his upper-left tile missing. undo_edit restored $3A.
